claims.text: The baseline alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can be maintained as a single-phase solid solution.
TiZrNbHfTa exhibits substantial local lattice distortion.
V is smaller in atomic radius than Zr.
Partially replacing Zr with V in HfNbTaTiZr increases the alloy's atomic size mismatch.
Increasing atomic size mismatch produces larger local lattice distortions.
Larger local lattice distortions act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion increases the energy barrier for dislocation slip.
Impeded dislocation motion increases hardness and yield strength.
Higher levels of V-for-Zr substitution will produce greater atomic misfit and monotonically higher hardness and yield strength than the baseline, provided the alloy remains single phase.
Homogenization at 1200°C followed by solution treatment and rapid quenching will retain the intended single-phase solid solution.
High-resolution TEM and XRD peak broadening can quantify the relevant local lattice distortion.
Electronic structure effects and phase transformations can affect dislocation mobility independently of simple atomic-size mismatch.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes compositions that undergo phase transformation or phase separation, but the falsification rule treats detected phase separation as falsification. Phase separation would instead place the sample outside the stated domain and would not by itself disprove the proposed distortion-strengthening mechanism.
